hypotheses.content: PE/EA condition response is scaffold-specific and can change sharply; V2 and interval width may enter a late tail at a different rate from V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The largest endpoint losses come from nonlinear late regimes. Local curves teach the retrained model where transitions occur and whether V1, V2, and width need separate condition interactions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new intermediate and high-condition labels reveal smooth interpolation, threshold behavior, or endpoint-specific transitions?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading setup can affect retention, but the effect is scaffold- and condition-dependent and cannot be inferred reliably from isolated measurements.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can prevent the retrained model from folding loading effects into solvent or scaffold effects, improving transfer to ordinary rows with different sample amounts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and mobile phase, are loading shifts consistent across early, intermediate, and long-retention scaffolds?

hypotheses.content: Transfer among positional isomers and heteroatom-rich aromatic scaffolds is uneven, so chemical representation coverage may fail even when broad functional-group descriptors look similar.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Paired m160/m161 and related aromatic labels can teach the model which local structural environments control silica retention beyond global polarity and H-bond counts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do paired positional-isomer measurements support a transferable response surface or require distinct scaffold-specific corrections?

hypotheses.content: High-CW and molecule-novel candidates in broad predicted regimes are useful repair points for sparse chemical-condition neighborhoods, especially when measured tail errors are large.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels can repair extrapolation and improve chemical transfer across the Row-distribution rather than only fitting dense, familiar scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which high-CW chemical environments produce labels that improve nearby unseen neighborhoods after retraining?

hypotheses.content: V1 and V2 require partly separate calibration: a model can be relatively close on one endpoint while missing the other, particularly in broad late intervals.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Training labels that expose endpoint asymmetry can improve the joint V1/V2 objective and reduce systematic V2 tail error without distorting V1 calibration.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the added curves reduce V2 residuals and interval-width errors without sacrificing V1 accuracy?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthens the nonlinear-response interpretation but weakens any global directional correction. For m159, the measured 10/1 point 79ff49052bce33597828 and 20/1 point a1dc71bed9d8f372c9e5 were substantially overpredicted, whereas the measured 50/1 point a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 was underpredicted, so the transition is not a simple uniform tail shift. m11 showed a similar change in behavior: c3c4fdce502f6d3576dc and 1182373ab8814dbe2f43 were close or moderately offset, while 6b8e53d2d8c8a90a7216 substantially underpredicted the 10/1 tail. The m114 result 44fcf641ccfa3b10a97c also confirms that V2 can remain badly calibrated after a condition shift. Matched loading outcomes remain mixed: m161 pairs 5258960e057b56ed51f8, 247846e36e9c012df30f, a60552f4d1a5ced4641f, and 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e, together with the m90 pair 29db30571b2a1ae59cc7 and 855832bd4005ac7abdc6, do not support a universal loading correction. I therefore prioritize paired loading labels and intermediate curves while retaining high-CW novel scaffolds for generalization repair.
batch_rationale: The batch combines five m159 points and paired m160/m161 labels to resolve the strongest condition-response and positional-isomer uncertainties, then adds m11, m114, and m90 curve points where recent feedback showed endpoint-specific tail behavior. Matched-loading experiments on m159, m11, m114, m78, m72, m37, m86, and m125 directly address the unresolved confounding between loading and mobile phase. The m211, m193, m198, m135, and m203 points extend measured tail families into intermediate conditions, while the molecule-novel m212, m119, m207, m206, m117, m204, and m178 rows probe chemically sparse neighborhoods with high CW distance. This gives the retrained QGeoGNN information about local nonlinear response, separate V1/V2 calibration, loading interactions, and chemical transfer across both familiar and undercovered portions of the Row-distribution.
